The CCEH gives its tunes as four-part scores; this page has the melody only, read from its MIDI file and checked against its incipit, and NoteFusion's engine wrote the solfa from the notes. It has not yet been checked against a printed hymn book. The arranger named above set CCEH's harmony, which is not shown here.

Questions about O Quanta Qualia

What is the doh of O Quanta Qualia?

In this version, in F major, doh is F. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does O Quanta Qualia start on?

It starts on d (F in F major). Find doh first, then sing up or down to d.

What words can be sung to O Quanta Qualia?

O Quanta Qualia is in the metre 10.10.10.10d: lines of 10, 10, 10, 10d syllables. Words written in the same metre fit it; check where the stresses fall before you sing them together.

Is O Quanta Qualia in the public domain?

Yes. Francois de La Feilee's work dates from 1808, John Bacchus Dykes died in 1876; the tune was first published in 1681. Everyone named died before 1955 and it was published before 1929, so the tune is out of copyright in the UK, the EU, the United States and Nigeria. Modern arrangements of it can still be under copyright.
